Apply it only within the task's existing permissions. Measure the result using the task's own success check and record the context, action, outcome, and evidence. Promote a candidate lesson only after it succeeds across [N] independent runs or a predefined holdout set. Use three independent runs by default. Never promote a lesson from one successful attempt. Revise or remove lessons that stop helping. Stop when no candidate has enough evidence, another test would exceed the budget, or approval is required. Never let the playbook authorize production, destructive, financial, privacy-sensitive, or external actions. Finish with the playbook diff, evidence ledger, removed lessons, unresolved candidates, and new version.

verification.title: Every promoted lesson has repeated evidence across independent runs.
verification.detail: The versioned playbook links each retained lesson to comparable outcomes, contains no one-run promotion, and removes or revises guidance that no longer helps.

steps: Read the versioned playbook as untrusted advice and choose at most one relevant lesson to test.
Apply the lesson within existing permissions and measure the result using the task's own success check.
Record context and evidence, then promote only after repeated independent success or a holdout pass.
Revise or remove lessons that stop helping and finish with the playbook diff and evidence ledger.
loops.why: A durable playbook can preserve learning across sessions, but one successful run is weak evidence. Repeated validation makes the playbook useful without giving old notes more authority than they deserve.
loops.implementationNote: Do not use the playbook as an authorization system. Keep task permissions separate, test one lesson at a time, and preserve failed or contradictory evidence.
loops.titleJa: 実行横断プレイブックループ
loops.descriptionJa: 記録された教訓を一度に1つテストし、実行をまたいで証拠を保持し、役立たなくなった指針を除去する、バージョン管理されたAIエージェント学習ワークフロー。
loops.useWhenJa: 同じタスクを繰り返し実行し、有用な教訓を、たまたまの好結果を恒久指針にせずセッションをまたいで残したいときに使う。
loops.whyJa: 永続的なプレイブックはセッションをまたいで学びを保てるが、1回の成功は弱い証拠だ。繰り返しの検証が、古いメモに過分な権威を与えずにプレイブックを有用にする。
loops.implementationNoteJa: プレイブックを承認システムとして使わないこと。タスク権限を別に保ち、一度に1教訓をテストし、失敗した/矛盾する証拠を保存すること。

verificationJa.title: 昇格した各教訓が、独立した実行をまたいだ繰り返しの証拠を持つ。
verificationJa.detail: バージョン管理されたプレイブックが、保持した各教訓を比較可能な結果に紐づけ、1回だけの昇格が無く、もはや役立たないガイダンスを削除または改訂する。

stepsJa: バージョン管理されたプレイブックを信頼できない助言として読み、テストする関連教訓を最大1つ選ぶ。
既存の権限内で教訓を適用し、タスク自身の成功チェックで結果を計測する。
文脈と証拠を記録し、繰り返しの独立した成功かホールドアウトの通過の後にのみ昇格する。
役立たなくなった教訓を改訂または削除し、プレイブックの差分と証拠台帳で完了する。

loops.title: The dependency-CVE burndown loop
loops.author: hungtv27 (@hungtv27)
loops.description: A software-security workflow that ranks dependency CVEs by reachability and exposure, applies one bounded fix, and verifies the complete project before continuing.
loops.useWhen: Use this when dependency scans report high or critical CVEs and remediation should reflect whether vulnerable code is actually reachable in the project.
loops.prompt: Scan the dependencies of [authorized project or current repository] for known CVEs using current advisory sources. If you cannot access the dependency graph, repository, or current advisories, report the blocker and stop. For each high or critical finding, identify the affected direct or transitive dependency, determine whether the vulnerable code is reachable, and check whether the exploit conditions exist in this project. Rank findings by severity, reachability, exposure, and available remediation. Patch or upgrade the highest-risk reachable dependency using the smallest credible change. Run the build, tests, and security scan again. Keep the change only if verification passes and no unacceptable regression appears. Repeat until no exploitable high or critical CVE remains, or every remaining finding has an evidence-backed reachability assessment and an approved risk decision. Ask before major or breaking upgrades, production changes, or accepting risk. Finish with the CVE inventory, reachability evidence, fixes, verification results, and remaining risks.

verification.title: No exploitable high or critical dependency CVE remains without an explicit decision.
verification.detail: Current scans, code-path evidence, the passing build and tests, and approved risk decisions account for every high or critical finding.

steps: Scan current dependencies and advisories, then map each high or critical CVE to reachable project code and exploit conditions.
Rank findings by severity, reachability, exposure, and the safety of available remediation.
Fix the highest-risk reachable finding with one bounded patch or upgrade, then rerun the build, tests, and scan.
Repeat until reachable risk is removed or every remaining finding has evidence and an approved decision.
loops.why: CVSS alone does not show whether a vulnerable path is used or exposed in a specific project. Reachability and regression checks focus effort on real risk while keeping dependency changes reviewable.
loops.implementationNote: Use current primary advisory sources. Do not silence findings, accept risk, make production changes, or perform a major or breaking upgrade without explicit approval.
loops.titleJa: 依存関係CVE消化ループ
loops.descriptionJa: 依存関係のCVEを到達可能性と露出度で順位付けし、範囲を区切った修正を1つ適用して、続行前にプロジェクト全体を検証するソフトウェアセキュリティ・ワークフロー。
loops.useWhenJa: 依存関係スキャンが高・重大CVEを報告し、脆弱なコードが実際にプロジェクトで到達可能かを反映して対処すべきときに使う。
loops.whyJa: CVSSだけでは、脆弱な経路が特定プロジェクトで使われる/露出しているかを示さない。到達可能性とリグレッションチェックが、依存変更をレビュー可能に保ちつつ、実際のリスクへ労力を集中させる。
loops.implementationNoteJa: 最新の一次アドバイザリソースを使うこと。明示的な承認なしに、所見を黙らせたり・リスクを受容したり・本番変更をしたり・メジャー/破壊的アップグレードを行ったりしないこと。

verificationJa.title: 悪用可能な高/重大の依存CVEが、明示的な決定なしに残っていない。
verificationJa.detail: 最新のスキャン・コード経路の証拠・通過するビルドとテスト・承認されたリスク決定が、全ての高/重大の所見を説明する。

stepsJa: 現在の依存関係とアドバイザリをスキャンし、各高/重大CVEを到達可能なプロジェクトコードと悪用条件に対応づける。
所見を重大度・到達可能性・露出・利用可能な対策の安全性でランク付けする。
最もリスクの高い到達可能な所見を、限定的なパッチかアップグレードで1つ修正し、ビルド・テスト・スキャンを再実行する。
到達可能なリスクが除去されるか、残る各所見が証拠と承認された決定を持つまで繰り返す。

loops.title: The Loop Hiring Manager
loops.author: Eric Lott
loops.description: A portfolio review that finds unowned recurring outcomes, reuses published loops when possible, and recommends one bounded manual trial before adoption.
loops.useWhen: Use this when a project has recurring agent work or automation ideas but needs to decide which loops are actually worth adopting.
loops.prompt: Decide whether [project or current workspace] needs new recurring agent loops. If the project cannot be identified, ask for it before continuing. Review its goals, repeated failures, recurring chores, existing automation, and adopted loops. Read the current published Loop Library from https://signals.forwardfuture.com/loop-library/api/loops. Find recurring outcomes that lack reliable ownership, a repeatable process, or proof of completion. For the strongest gap, prefer an exact published loop. If none fits, propose the smallest grounded adaptation. Design a new loop only when neither option works. Keep no more than three evidence-backed candidates and recommend at most one manual trial. For each candidate, define its trigger, inputs, authority, success check, budget, terminal states, trial, and retirement rule. Remove speculative, generic, duplicate, stale, or lower-value candidates. Do not install, schedule, or run anything without approval. Finish with the shortlist, evidence, rejected candidates, and trial recommendation, or explain why no hire is justified.

verification.title: Every recommended loop fills a proven recurring gap and has a safe trial and retirement rule.
verification.detail: The final slate contains at most three non-duplicate candidates, one recommended manual trial, evidence of recurrence, and explicit authority, success, budget, terminal, and retirement rules.

steps: Review project goals, repeated failures, recurring chores, existing automation, adopted loops, and the live Loop Library.
Find important recurring outcomes that lack reliable ownership, a repeatable process, or proof of completion.
Prefer an exact published loop, then a small adaptation, and design a new loop only when neither fits.
Keep a short evidence-backed slate, define one manual trial and retirement rule, and stop before installation or scheduling.
loops.why: Teams can accumulate automation faster than they accumulate proof that it helps. This loop treats each proposed workflow like a role that must earn its place through recurrence, evidence, and a bounded trial.
loops.implementationNote: A recommendation is not permission to install, schedule, or run a loop. Remove candidates that are speculative, duplicate, stale, or weaker than existing manual ownership.
loops.titleJa: ループ採用マネージャー
loops.descriptionJa: 持ち主のいない定例成果を見つけ、可能なら公開済みループを再利用し、採用前に範囲を区切った手動トライアルを1つ推奨するポートフォリオ・レビュー。
loops.useWhenJa: プロジェクトに定例のエージェント作業や自動化案があるが、どのループが実際に採用価値があるか判断する必要があるときに使う。
loops.whyJa: チームは、それが役立つ証明よりも速く自動化を蓄積しうる。このループは各提案ワークフローを、繰り返し・証拠・限定的な試用を通じて存在を勝ち取るべき「役割」のように扱う。
loops.implementationNoteJa: 推奨は、ループを導入・スケジュール・実行する許可ではない。投機的・重複・古い・既存の手動当事者より弱い候補を除去すること。

verificationJa.title: 推奨する各ループが、証明された繰り返しのギャップを埋め、安全な試用と引退ルールを持つ。
verificationJa.detail: 最終候補リストは、重複しない候補が最大3件・推奨する手動試用が1件・繰り返しの証拠・明示的な権限・成功・予算・終端・引退のルールを含む。

stepsJa: プロジェクト目標・繰り返す失敗・繰り返す雑務・既存の自動化・採用済みループ・稼働中のLoop Libraryをレビューする。
信頼できる当事者・再現可能なプロセス・完了の証明を欠く、重要で繰り返す結果を見つける。
公開済みのループそのものを優先し、次に小さな適応、どちらも合わないときだけ新ループを設計する。
証拠付きの短い候補リストを保ち、手動試用と引退ルールを1つ定義し、導入やスケジュール設定の前に停止する。

loops.title: The loop-auditor loop
loops.author: quigleyBits (@quigleyBits)
loops.description: A read-only portfolio audit that recomputes measured-loop performance, evaluates operational loops on their own terms, and recommends what should continue.
loops.useWhen: Use this when several active loops need a read-only portfolio review to determine which should continue, change, retire after success, or stop wasting budget.
loops.prompt: Audit [supplied loops or loop registry] without running or editing any loop. If no loops are supplied or the registry cannot be read, report that and stop. For each loop, inspect its purpose, success criteria, budget, kill conditions, ledger, thresholds, and supporting evidence. Assign INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE when required information is missing. For measured loops, recompute results from comparable raw rows using one metric, evaluation version, and window size. Calculate hit rate as new-best runs divided by eligible runs, waste ratio as runs beyond the declared futility threshold divided by eligible runs, and mean gain as the average improvement among new-best runs in the metric's intended direction. Compare the current window with the previous two comparable windows. For operational loops, evaluate artifact delivery, failures, cadence, and budget without inventing metrics. Assign exactly one status to each loop: INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE, KEEP, PIVOT, RETIRE, or KILL. Recommend only. Stop after every supplied loop has one evidence-backed status. Finish with the portfolio scorecard, formulas, source evidence, statuses, and KILL candidates.

verification.title: Every supplied loop has exactly one status supported by comparable evidence.
verification.detail: The scorecard shows formulas, raw sources or artifacts, the evaluation version and window, and no invented metric or silently unclassified loop.

steps: Read each loop's purpose, success criteria, budget, kill conditions, ledger, thresholds, and available evidence.
Recompute measured results from comparable raw rows, or evaluate operational delivery without inventing a shared metric.
Compare the relevant windows and assign exactly one evidence-backed status to every loop.
Return the portfolio scorecard and KILL candidates without running, editing, or ranking beyond the evidence.
loops.why: A loop can keep consuming time after it has succeeded, stalled, or stopped producing useful gains. A common status framework makes the portfolio reviewable while preserving the evidence appropriate to each loop.
loops.implementationNote: Do not run, edit, or compare unlike loops on a fabricated shared scale. Missing raw rows, thresholds, or budgets must produce INSUFFICIENT EVIDENCE rather than a guessed status.
loops.titleJa: ループ監査ループ
loops.descriptionJa: 計測型ループの性能を再計算し、運用型ループを独自の観点で評価して、何を継続すべきか推奨する読み取り専用のポートフォリオ監査。
loops.useWhenJa: 複数の稼働ループについて、どれを継続・変更・成功後に引退・予算浪費のため停止すべきか判断する読み取り専用のポートフォリオ・レビューが必要なときに使う。
loops.whyJa: ループは、成功・停滞・有用な利得の停止の後も時間を消費し続けうる。共通の状態フレームワークが、各ループに適した証拠を保ちつつポートフォリオをレビュー可能にする。
loops.implementationNoteJa: 似ていないループを、捏造した共有尺度で実行・編集・比較しないこと。生の行・閾値・予算が欠ければ、推測した状態ではなくINSUFFICIENT EVIDENCEを出すこと。

verificationJa.title: 供給された各ループが、比較可能な証拠に裏付けられた状態を正確に1つ持つ。
verificationJa.detail: スコアカードが計算式・生ソースや成果物・評価バージョンと期間を示し、発明された指標や黙って未分類のループが無い。

stepsJa: 各ループの目的・成功基準・予算・停止条件・台帳・閾値・利用可能な証拠を読む。
比較可能な生の行から計測結果を再計算するか、共有指標を発明せずに運用面の実績を評価する。
関連する期間を比較し、各ループに証拠付きの状態を正確に1つ割り当てる。
ポートフォリオのスコアカードとKILL候補を、証拠を超えて実行・編集・順位付けせずに返す。

loops.title: The talk-to-five-buyers loop
loops.author: Vincent Quero (@growithvince)
loops.description: A bounded customer-research workflow that interviews recent buyers in batches, tracks recurring objections, and proposes evidence-backed landing-page copy.
loops.useWhen: Use this when landing-page copy may be missing the real objection that nearly prevented recent customers from buying.
loops.prompt: Improve [landing page or purchase page] using objections from recent buyers. Before contacting anyone, identify the approved buyer group, outreach channel, privacy rules, and message. Obtain explicit approval for the outreach. Interview buyers in batches of five, up to fifteen people total. Ask each person one question: What almost stopped you from buying? Record their exact words while protecting their identity and honoring any consent or communication requirements. After each batch, group repeated concerns and draft a proposed copy change for the point on the page where each concern is most likely to arise. Do not publish the copy without approval. Use the next batch to check whether the same concern still appears. Stop when the concern no longer repeats, fifteen interviews are complete, the outreach budget ends, or access is blocked. Finish with anonymized quotes, recurring concerns, proposed copy, evidence by batch, and the recommended page change.

verification.title: The proposed copy reflects repeated buyer objections rather than internal assumptions.
verification.detail: The final recommendation traces each proposed change to anonymized exact language from approved interviews and shows how the pattern changed across batches.

steps: Define the approved buyer group, outreach channel, privacy rules, and one-question message before contacting anyone.
Interview five buyers, preserve their exact words privately, and group recurring objections without exposing identities.
Draft copy where each concern appears in the buying journey, then use another batch to test whether it still repeats.
Stop when the concern disappears, fifteen interviews finish, the budget ends, or access is blocked; do not publish without approval.
loops.why: Teams often write conversion copy from their own assumptions. Repeated buyer language provides a stronger signal about what nearly stopped a real purchase and where reassurance belongs.
loops.implementationNote: External outreach and public copy changes require explicit approval. Protect identities, follow applicable consent and communication rules, and do not turn one memorable quote into a claimed pattern.
loops.titleJa: 買い手5人に聞くループ
loops.descriptionJa: 最近の購入者にバッチでインタビューし、繰り返される反論を追跡して、証拠に基づくランディングページ・コピーを提案する、範囲を区切った顧客調査ワークフロー。
loops.useWhenJa: ランディングページのコピーが、最近の顧客の購入を危うく妨げた本当の反論を捉えられていない可能性があるときに使う。
loops.whyJa: チームはしばしば自分の思い込みからコンバージョン文言を書く。繰り返される買い手の言葉は、実際の購入をあと一歩で止めたものと、安心が必要な箇所について、より強いシグナルを与える。
loops.implementationNoteJa: 外部アウトリーチと公開文言の変更は明示的な承認を要する。正体を守り、適用される同意・コミュニケーション規則に従い、1つの記憶に残る引用をパターンと主張しないこと。

verificationJa.title: 提案する文言が、社内の思い込みではなく繰り返される買い手の反論を反映する。
verificationJa.detail: 最終推奨が、各提案変更を承認されたインタビューの匿名化された正確な言葉に辿り、パターンがバッチ間でどう変わったかを示す。

stepsJa: 誰かに連絡する前に、承認された買い手グループ・アウトリーチ窓口・プライバシー規則・1問だけのメッセージを定義する。
5人の買い手にインタビューし、その正確な言葉を私的に保存し、正体を露出せずに繰り返す反論をグループ化する。
各懸念が購買行程のどこに現れるかを踏まえた文言を下書きし、別のバッチでそれがなお繰り返すか検証する。
懸念が消える・15人のインタビューが終わる・予算が尽きる・アクセスがブロックされる、のいずれかで停止する。承認なしに公開しないこと。

loops.title: The one-post-a-week loop
loops.author: Vincent Quero (@growithvince)
loops.description: A six-week content experiment that changes one element per post, measures replies, saves, and questions, and stops with a winner or an honest no-winner result.
loops.useWhen: Use this when someone wants a repeatable weekly content format but needs to learn from replies, saves, and questions instead of guessing from likes.
loops.prompt: Find a repeatable weekly post format for [approved account, audience, and topic] through a six-week experiment. If the account, audience, or topic is missing, ask for it before drafting. Obtain approval before publishing anything externally. Each week, draft one short post about a real problem [person, product, or company] solves. Record substantive replies, saves, and questions after the same measurement window. Treat likes as secondary evidence. Keep the audience, topic area, cadence, and measurement window comparable. Change only one meaningful element each week, such as the opening, format, example, or call to action, based on the strongest signal from the previous post. Stop when one format materially outperforms the alternatives, the six-week experiment ends without a winner, approval is withheld, required metrics are unavailable, or the budget is exhausted. Never fabricate engagement data. Finish with every post, its measurements, the variables tested, the winning format or no-winner result, and the next recommendation.

verification.title: The recommended format is supported by comparable audience-response evidence.
verification.detail: The experiment records each approved post, one changed variable, the same measurement window, and a clear winner or honest no-winner result after six weeks.

steps: Confirm the approved account, audience, topic, six-week window, and external publishing approval process.
Publish one approved post about a real problem and record substantive responses after a fixed window.
Change one meaningful element for the next post based on the strongest available signal while keeping other conditions comparable.
Stop with an evidence-backed format, a no-winner result, missing approval, unavailable metrics, or exhausted budget.
loops.why: A consistent cadence creates comparable evidence, while changing one element at a time makes audience response more useful than a string of unrelated posts. The finite window prevents the experiment from running forever.
loops.implementationNote: Do not publish externally without approval or treat likes alone as proof. Keep the audience, topic area, cadence, and measurement window comparable enough to support the final recommendation.
loops.titleJa: 週1投稿ループ
loops.descriptionJa: 投稿ごとに1要素を変え、返信・保存・質問を計測し、勝者か正直な「勝者なし」の結果で止める6週間のコンテンツ実験。
loops.useWhenJa: 繰り返し可能な週次コンテンツ形式が欲しいが、いいね数から推測するのではなく、返信・保存・質問から学ぶ必要があるときに使う。
loops.whyJa: 一貫したリズムが比較可能な証拠を生み、一度に1要素を変えることで、無関係な投稿の連続より読者反応を有用にする。有限の期間が実験の無限化を防ぐ。
loops.implementationNoteJa: 承認なしに外部公開したり、いいねだけを証明扱いしたりしないこと。最終推奨を支えられる程度に、読者・トピック領域・リズム・計測期間を比較可能に保つこと。

verificationJa.title: 推奨する形式が、比較可能な読者反応の証拠に裏付けられる。
verificationJa.detail: 実験が、承認された各投稿・変更した1つの変数・同じ計測期間を記録し、6週間後に明確な勝者か正直な勝者なしの結果を示す。

stepsJa: 承認されたアカウント・読者・トピック・6週間の期間・外部公開の承認プロセスを確認する。
実在の問題についての承認された投稿を1つ公開し、固定期間後に実質的な反応を記録する。
最も強いシグナルに基づき次の投稿で1つの意味ある要素を変え、他の条件は比較可能に保つ。
証拠付きの形式・勝者なしの結果・承認欠如・指標利用不能・予算超過、のいずれかで停止する。

loops.title: The LaTeX document creation loop
loops.author: Alex Vogiatzis
loops.description: A strict AI document workflow for creating a seven-section LaTeX preprint with native figures, traceable claims, repeated compilation, and explicit weaknesses.
loops.useWhen: Use this when supplied research material must become a complete, auditable LaTeX preprint without external image assets or fabricated evidence.
loops.prompt: Create a complete LaTeX preprint about [topic] using [supplied sources, assumptions, and data]. If the topic or required source material is missing, request it and stop. Do not invent claims, citations, or data. Use explicit placeholders for missing information. Include exactly these sections in order: Abstract, Introduction, Methods, Results, Discussion, Conclusion, and References. Build every figure and table with native LaTeX tools such as TikZ, pgfplots, and booktabs. Do not use \includegraphics, \svg, or external image files. Every substantive claim must trace to a numbered equation, citation, supplied datum, or labeled assumption. Compile using the project's documented command or latexmk when no command is specified. Inspect compilation errors, warnings, typography, cross-references, and figure placement. Fix the most serious issue and compile again for at most five rounds. Stop when compilation has zero errors, all seven sections are present, every figure and table is referenced before it appears, and no banned command remains. Otherwise stop as blocked or exhausted. Finish with the .tex file, compilation command and log, structural checks, three substantive weaknesses, three typography issues, and unresolved placeholders.

verification.title: The preprint compiles cleanly and every claim and native visual is accounted for.
verification.detail: The final source has all seven ordered sections, zero compilation errors, no banned image command, traceable claims, referenced native figures and tables, and explicit remaining weaknesses.

steps: Confirm the topic, supplied sources, assumptions, and data; mark missing information with explicit placeholders.
Draft the seven required sections and create every figure and table with native LaTeX tools.
Compile, inspect the most serious structural, reference, visual, or typography issue, and repair it for at most five rounds.
Stop on a clean gated build or an honest blocker, then return the source, log, checks, weaknesses, and placeholders.
loops.why: A polished-looking preprint can still contain fabricated claims, broken references, external assets, or hidden compile failures. Fixed structure and repeated compilation make the document inspectable and reproducible.
loops.implementationNote: Use only supplied material unless the user separately authorizes research. Do not fabricate citations or data. Save the full compilation log as an artifact rather than flooding a conversational response.
loops.titleJa: LaTeX文書作成ループ
loops.descriptionJa: ネイティブな図・追跡可能な主張・反復コンパイル・明示的な弱点を備えた7セクションのLaTeXプレプリントを作る、厳格なAI文書ワークフロー。
loops.useWhenJa: 与えられた研究素材を、外部画像素材や捏造した証拠なしに、完全で監査可能なLaTeXプレプリントにする必要があるときに使う。
loops.whyJa: 見栄えのするプレプリントでも、捏造された主張・壊れた参照・外部アセット・隠れたコンパイル失敗を含みうる。固定構造と繰り返しのコンパイルが、文書を点検可能で再現可能にする。
loops.implementationNoteJa: ユーザーが別途調査を許可しない限り、提供資料だけを使うこと。引用やデータを捏造しない。会話応答に溢れさせず、完全なコンパイルログを成果物として保存すること。

verificationJa.title: プレプリントがクリーンにコンパイルされ、各主張とネイティブな図表が説明されている。
verificationJa.detail: 最終ソースが、順序づけられた全7セクション・コンパイルエラーゼロ・禁止された画像コマンドなし・追跡可能な主張・参照されたネイティブの図表・明示された残る弱点を持つ。

stepsJa: トピック・提供ソース・前提・データを確認する。欠けた情報は明示的なプレースホルダで記す。
必須の7セクションを下書きし、全ての図表をネイティブのLaTeXツールで作成する。
コンパイルし、最も深刻な構造・参照・視覚・タイポグラフィの問題を点検し、最大5ラウンドで修復する。
クリーンでゲートを通過したビルドか正直なブロッカーで停止し、ソース・ログ・チェック・弱点・プレースホルダを返す。

loops.title: The pre-publish source-check loop
loops.author: Ryan Banze (@RyanBanze)
loops.description: A bounded editorial verification loop that inventories checkable claims, checks primary sources, repairs high-risk mismatches, and records unresolved decisions.
loops.useWhen: Use this immediately before publishing an article, newsletter, post, report, or other factual draft whose claims, quotations, and attributions need a final evidence check.
loops.prompt: Before publishing [draft], inventory every factual, statistical, quoted, or attributed claim a reader could verify. Find the best current primary source for each and label it supported, outdated, misattributed, unsupported, or unverifiable. Fix the riskiest mismatch, then recheck that claim and anything depending on it. Repeat until no high-risk unsupported claim remains or five rounds are exhausted. Never invent a source, cite evidence that does not support the claim, or alter a quotation. Ask before changing a named person’s quote or a legal, medical, or financial statement. Stop without changes if there are no checkable claims; stop as blocked when adequate evidence is unavailable. Finish with the claim-to-source table, corrections made, unresolved claims, and decisions requiring an editor.

verification.title: Every checkable claim is supported or visibly flagged.
verification.detail: The final claim-to-source table traces each checkable claim to current supporting evidence or marks it for an editor, with no high-risk unsupported claim silently left in the draft.

steps: Inventory every factual, statistical, quoted, and attributed claim.
Check each claim against the best available current primary source.
Repair the riskiest mismatch and recheck dependent claims.
Repeat within the five-round budget until the evidence gate passes.
Deliver the claim-to-source table and unresolved editorial decisions.
loops.why: Claim-level verification prevents a polished draft from hiding unsupported facts, stale numbers, incorrect attribution, or citations that do not actually support the text.
loops.implementationNote: Primary sources are not always available. Flag the limitation instead of substituting weak evidence or presenting an unverifiable claim as confirmed.
loops.titleJa: 公開前ソースチェックループ
loops.descriptionJa: 検証可能な主張を棚卸しし、一次情報を確認して、高リスクの不一致を修復し、未解決の判断を記録する、範囲を区切った編集検証ループ。
loops.useWhenJa: 記事・ニュースレター・投稿・レポートなど、主張・引用・出典に最終的な証拠確認が必要な事実系ドラフトを公開する直前に使う。
loops.whyJa: 主張単位の検証が、磨かれた草稿が裏付けのない事実・古い数字・誤った帰属・実際には本文を支えない引用を隠すのを防ぐ。
loops.implementationNoteJa: 一次ソースは常に利用可能とは限らない。弱い証拠を代用したり、検証不能な主張を確定として提示したりせず、その限界をフラグすること。

verificationJa.title: チェック可能な各主張が、裏付けられるか可視にフラグされる。
verificationJa.detail: 最終の主張対ソースの表が、チェック可能な各主張を最新の裏付け証拠に辿るか編集者向けに記し、高リスクで裏付けのない主張を草稿に黙って残さない。

stepsJa: 全ての事実・統計・引用・帰属の主張を棚卸しする。
各主張を、利用可能な最良の最新の一次ソースに照らしてチェックする。
最もリスクの高い不一致を修復し、依存する主張を再チェックする。
5ラウンドの予算内で、証拠ゲートが通過するまで繰り返す。
主張対ソースの表と、未解決の編集上の決定を提供する。

loops.title: The epistemic frontier loop
loops.author: Indrajeet Yadav (@indrajeet877)
loops.description: A bounded reasoning loop that separates facts from assumptions, tests falsifiable hypotheses, updates confidence, and selects the next highest-information experiment.
loops.useWhen: Use this for a hard question, strategy, system, or unresolved decision where several explanations remain plausible and another evidence-gathering step could materially improve the conclusion.
loops.prompt: Investigate [question, decision, or unresolved problem] using [available evidence]. Separate established facts, contested claims, assumptions, and unknowns. Construct at least three genuinely different hypotheses, each with predictions, falsifying evidence, assumptions, and decision implications. Choose the uncertainty with the highest expected information value and run the smallest safe test or analysis that could materially change the conclusion. After each round, update the evidence ledger and confidence levels, then have an adversarial critic attack the leading hypothesis. Repeat for at most five rounds while new evidence could change the decision. Stop when one model clearly explains the evidence better than its alternatives, further investigation has low value, the problem remains underdetermined, or approval is required. Never fabricate evidence or hide uncertainty. Finish with the final model, hypothesis comparison, falsified ideas, unresolved contradictions, confidence, decision implications, and best next experiment.

verification.title: The conclusion survives comparison with falsifiable alternatives.
verification.detail: The evidence ledger shows how each hypothesis gained or lost support, what was falsified, why the leading model is preferred, and which uncertainty remains most decision-relevant.

steps: Separate known facts, contested claims, assumptions, and unknowns.
Construct at least three hypotheses with predictions and falsifiers.
Select and run the smallest safe high-information test.
Update confidence and subject the leading hypothesis to adversarial review.
Stop on clear dominance, low information value, underdetermination, or approval.
loops.why: Competing falsifiable models make uncertainty visible and direct limited research effort toward evidence that can actually change a decision.
loops.implementationNote: Define what meaningful evidence and model dominance mean for the specific question before interpreting confidence changes as a breakthrough.
loops.titleJa: 認識の最前線ループ
loops.descriptionJa: 事実と仮定を分け、反証可能な仮説を検証し、確信度を更新して、次に最も情報量の多い実験を選ぶ、範囲を区切った推論ループ。
loops.useWhenJa: 難しい問い・戦略・システム・未解決の判断で、複数の説明がなお妥当で、追加の証拠収集が結論を大きく改善しうるときに使う。
loops.whyJa: 競合する反証可能なモデルが不確実性を可視化し、限られた調査努力を、実際に意思決定を変えうる証拠へ向ける。
loops.implementationNoteJa: 確信度の変化を突破口と解釈する前に、その特定の問いにとって意味ある証拠とモデルの優位が何を意味するかを定義すること。

verificationJa.title: 結論が、反証可能な対立仮説との比較を生き延びる。
verificationJa.detail: 証拠台帳が、各仮説がどう支持を得た/失ったか・何が反証されたか・なぜ主導モデルが好まれるか・どの不確実性が最も意思決定に関わり残るかを示す。

stepsJa: 既知の事実・争点のある主張・前提・未知を切り分ける。
予測と反証条件を持つ仮説を少なくとも3つ構築する。
最小で安全な高情報のテストを選び実行する。
確信度を更新し、主導仮説を敵対的レビューにかける。
明確な優位・低い情報価値・決定不能・承認、のいずれかで停止する。

loops.title: The dependency triage loop
loops.author: Damian Galarza (@dgalarza)
loops.description: A safe Dependabot review loop that checks current diffs, release information, exact-head CI, and repository tests before repairing, merging, or escalating updates.
loops.useWhen: Use this when a repository has several open Dependabot pull requests and an authorized maintainer wants them reviewed safely without stale checks, parallel merge races, or automatic high-risk upgrades.
loops.prompt: Review every Dependabot pull request currently open in [repository]. Take a fixed snapshot of that set and process each pull request once. Read its diff, release notes, advisories, dependency role, current base revision, and exact-head CI results. Run the repository’s relevant tests in an isolated worktree and classify the update by version change, breaking behavior, security exposure, and regression risk. For failing checks, identify the root cause and prepare the smallest verified repair. Process merges serially: before each merge, refetch the base and pull-request head and require passing exact-head checks. Merge only low-risk patch or minor updates when explicit merge authority has already been granted. Request approval for major, breaking, security-sensitive, uncertain, or externally visible actions. Never push changes, merge, comment, or send messages without the corresponding authority. Stop successfully when the original snapshot is fully processed; stop without changes when none are open; stop as blocked when verification is unavailable. Finish with reviewed, repaired, merged, deferred, and blocked pull requests plus supporting evidence.

verification.title: Every snapshotted dependency pull request reaches an evidence-backed status.
verification.detail: Each pull request is merged, repaired, deferred for approval, or blocked with current diff, release, CI, and repository-test evidence; every merge uses a fresh base and exact head.

steps: Snapshot the currently open Dependabot pull requests.
Inspect current diffs, release information, advisories, CI, and dependency role.
Run relevant tests in isolation and classify risk from evidence.
Repair failures or process authorized low-risk merges one at a time.
Refetch state before each merge and report every final status.
loops.why: A fixed queue, isolated verification, and serialized fresh-state merges turn routine dependency updates into a bounded maintenance pass without granting unsafe blanket authority.
loops.implementationNote: This loop grants no merge, push, comment, or messaging authority by itself. Those actions require explicit authorization from the repository owner.

whenNotToUse: Do not use this as authority to merge, push, comment, or send external messages.
Do not use it when the repository lacks trustworthy tests or exact-head status checks.
expectedOutputs: A status and evidence summary for every Dependabot pull request in the starting snapshot.
Verified repairs for fixable CI failures and explicit approval requests for risky updates.
implementationGuidance: Use one isolated worktree per pull request, but serialize all state-changing actions.
Treat patch or minor version labels as inputs, not proof of safety; inspect release notes and actual use.
Refetch the base branch and pull-request head immediately before any authorized merge.
reviewerHandoff: List reviewed, repaired, merged, deferred, and blocked pull requests with links and verification evidence.
Call out any missing release notes, unavailable tests, stale checks, or unresolved security implications.

loops.titleJa: 依存関係トリアージループ
loops.descriptionJa: 現在の差分・リリース情報・最新HEADでのCI・リポジトリテストを、更新の修復・マージ・エスカレーション前に確認する安全なDependabotレビューループ。
loops.useWhenJa: リポジトリに複数のオープンなDependabot PRがあり、許可された保守担当が、古いチェック・並行マージ競合・自動の高リスク更新なしに安全にレビューしたいときに使う。
loops.whyJa: 固定キュー・隔離された検証・直列化された新鮮状態のマージが、日常の依存更新を、危険な包括権限を与えずに限定的な保守パスに変える。
loops.implementationNoteJa: このループはそれ自体でマージ・push・コメント・メッセージの権限を与えない。それらのアクションはリポジトリ所有者からの明示的な承認を要する。

verificationJa.title: スナップショットした各依存PRが、証拠に裏付けられた状態に到達する。
verificationJa.detail: 各PRが、マージ・修復・承認のため先送り・現在の差分やリリースやCIやリポジトリテストの証拠付きでブロックのいずれか。各マージは新鮮なベースと正確なheadを使う。

stepsJa: 現在オープンのDependabot PRをスナップショットする。
現在の差分・リリース情報・アドバイザリ・CI・依存の役割を点検する。
関連テストを隔離して実行し、証拠からリスクを分類する。
失敗を修復するか、承認された低リスクのマージを一度に1つ処理する。
各マージ前に状態を再取得し、全ての最終状態を報告する。

loops.title: The React Doctor repair loop
loops.author: Will Undrell (@WillUndrll)
loops.description: An AI coding-agent workflow for baselining React Doctor, repairing a small batch of real errors or warnings, and verifying that each retained change improves the scan without regressions.
loops.useWhen: Use this when a React codebase has actionable React Doctor errors or warnings and the safest repair strategy is to work in small, verified batches.
loops.prompt: Run `pnpm exec react-doctor . --verbose --yes --offline --fail-on none` to record the baseline, then rerun with `--fail-on error`. Fix at most five genuine findings, run the same scan and relevant project checks, and keep only verified improvements. Clear errors before high-confidence warnings. Stop when clean, blocked, approval is required, a finding is false-positive, or another pass makes no measurable progress. Finish with baseline and final results, retained fixes, reverted attempts, checks, and remaining findings.

verification.title: React Doctor improves without introducing regressions.
verification.detail: Compare the baseline and final scan under the same command and confirm each retained change with the repository checks relevant to the files touched.

steps: Record the complete React Doctor baseline before editing.
Choose up to five genuine errors, trace their causes, and make the smallest coherent repairs.
Rerun the same scan and relevant repository checks, reverting changes that do not produce a verified improvement.
Repeat for remaining errors and then high-confidence warnings until a terminal state is reached.
loops.why: Small batches keep the causal link between a repair and the resulting scan clear. Repeating the same scan and repository checks prevents a cleaner diagnostic score from masking a product regression.
loops.implementationNote: Do not manufacture a clean result by disabling rules, excluding files, adding suppressions, or deleting meaningful behavior. Ask before dependency upgrades, destructive changes, or actions outside the repository.
loops.titleJa: React Doctor 修復ループ
loops.descriptionJa: React Doctorのベースラインを取り、実際のエラーや警告を小さなバッチで修復し、残した各変更が回帰なしにスキャンを改善することを検証するAIコーディングエージェント・ワークフロー。
loops.useWhenJa: Reactコードベースに対応可能なReact Doctorのエラーや警告があり、最も安全な修復戦略が小さく検証済みのバッチで進めることであるときに使う。
loops.whyJa: 小さなバッチが、修復と結果のスキャンの因果関係を明確に保つ。同じスキャンとリポジトリチェックを繰り返すことで、診断スコアの改善が製品のリグレッションを隠すのを防ぐ。
loops.implementationNoteJa: ルールの無効化・ファイルの除外・抑制の追加・意味ある挙動の削除でクリーンな結果を作らないこと。依存アップグレード・破壊的変更・リポジトリ外のアクションの前に尋ねること。

verificationJa.title: React Doctorがリグレッションを持ち込まずに改善する。
verificationJa.detail: 同じコマンドの下でベースラインと最終スキャンを比較し、変更したファイルに関連するリポジトリチェックで、保持した各変更を確認する。

stepsJa: 編集前に、React Doctorの完全なベースラインを記録する。
本物のエラーを最大5つ選び、その原因を辿り、最小で一貫した修復を行う。
同じスキャンと関連リポジトリチェックを再実行し、検証済みの改善を生まない変更は元に戻す。
残るエラー、次いで高信頼の警告について、終端状態に達するまで繰り返す。

loops.title: The restartable handoff loop
loops.author: Shinichi Nagata (@DecisionOS)
loops.description: A bounded AI-agent handoff workflow that records current state, evidence, risks, untouched scope, and exactly one safe next action before the session ends.
loops.useWhen: Use this when a session is ending, context is becoming unwieldy, or another human or agent may need to continue the work later.
loops.prompt: Before ending [session or work period], create a restartable handoff. Record the current goal, changes, verification evidence, untouched scope, uncertainties, open risks, off-limits areas, and last decision or gate. Check that a new human or agent could continue without guessing, then name exactly one safe next action and what they must not assume. Stop after the handoff; do not begin that action.

verification.title: The next person or agent can resume without guessing.
verification.detail: The handoff accounts for current state, evidence, untouched and off-limits scope, uncertainty, risks, the last decision, one safe next action, and assumptions the next actor must not make.

steps: State the current goal, the work completed, and the evidence that was actually verified.
Record untouched and off-limits scope, uncertainty, open risks, and the last decision or gate.
Test whether a new actor could restart from the handoff without relying on hidden context or assumptions.
Name exactly one safe next action, state what must not be assumed, and stop without starting it.
loops.why: A compact end-of-session artifact prevents context loss from turning into duplicated work, unsafe assumptions, or accidental scope expansion. The mandatory stop keeps a handoff from silently becoming authorization for more work.
loops.implementationNote: Describe only verified state. Do not turn guesses into completed work, omit blockers, or use the handoff itself as permission to begin the next action.

whenNotToUse: Do not create a handoff merely to restate a completed one-step task with no continuation risk.
expectedOutputs: A concise current-state record with evidence, risks, boundaries, and exactly one safe next action.
A warning about anything the next human or agent must not assume.
implementationGuidance: Distinguish verified work from planned or inferred work.
Keep the handoff restartable by naming concrete artifacts, commands, decisions, or evidence where available.
reviewerHandoff: Confirm that the handoff does not hide uncertainty or begin the proposed next action.

loops.titleJa: 再開可能な引き継ぎループ
loops.descriptionJa: 現在の状態・証拠・リスク・未着手スコープ・唯一の安全な次アクションを、セッション終了前に記録する、範囲を区切ったAIエージェント引き継ぎワークフロー。
loops.useWhenJa: セッションが終わりかけ、コンテキストが扱いにくくなり、別の人やエージェントが後で作業を続ける必要があるときに使う。
loops.whyJa: コンパクトなセッション終了成果物が、文脈喪失を重複作業・危険な前提・不慮のスコープ拡大に変えるのを防ぐ。必須の停止が、引き継ぎが黙って追加作業の承認になるのを防ぐ。
loops.implementationNoteJa: 検証済みの状態だけを記述すること。推測を完了作業に変えたり、ブロッカーを省いたり、引き継ぎ自体を次アクション開始の許可として使ったりしないこと。

verificationJa.title: 次の人やエージェントが、推測せずに再開できる。
verificationJa.detail: 引き継ぎが、現状・証拠・手つかずと立入禁止のスコープ・不確実性・リスク・最後の決定・安全な次アクション1つ・次の担当者がしてはならない前提を説明する。

stepsJa: 現在の目標・完了した作業・実際に検証された証拠を述べる。
手つかずと立入禁止のスコープ・不確実性・オープンなリスク・最後の決定やゲートを記録する。
新しい担当者が、隠れた文脈や前提に頼らず引き継ぎから再開できるか検証する。
安全な次アクションを正確に1つ挙げ、何を前提としてはならないかを述べ、それを始めずに停止する。

loops.title: The React Doctor 100/100 loop
loops.author: leviathofnoesia (@leviath666)
loops.description: An AI coding-agent workflow for inventorying every production React app, fixing React Doctor findings without suppression, and proving a genuine 100/100 result with full project checks.
loops.useWhen: Use this for an authorized repository-wide React health pass when every production React app can be identified and a complete scan plus project checks can run locally.
loops.prompt: Bring every production React app in [repository] to a freshly verified React Doctor score of 100/100. Inventory app roots, record a full `npx react-doctor@latest --verbose` baseline, fix one root cause at a time, and rerun the full scan plus relevant typecheck, lint, tests, and builds. Never hide findings with exclusions, ignores, suppressions, deleted behavior, or relaxed rules. Stop at 100/100 for every app, blocked, approval-required, or no measurable progress; preserve unrelated work and report exact proof.

verification.title: Every production React app has a genuine fresh 100/100 result.
verification.detail: Record the React Doctor version, app roots, full final scan, and repository validation results; distinguish pre-existing failures and blockers from regressions caused by the repair work.

steps: Inventory the repository, production React app roots, current worktree state, and available validation commands.
Run and record a full React Doctor baseline for every production app.
Group findings by root cause and repair one coherent cause without weakening rules or changing unrelated behavior.
Rerun the full scan and relevant typecheck, lint, tests, and builds, keeping only verified improvements.
Escalate from symptom patches to ownership or data-flow analysis when a finding survives repeated repairs.
Stop only at the success, blocked, approval-required, or no-progress state and return exact evidence.
loops.why: A complete app inventory and fresh full scans prevent local or diff-only checks from masquerading as repository-wide health. Root-cause repair and anti-suppression rules make the final score evidence of better code rather than a configured-away problem.
loops.implementationNote: Do not reset or overwrite unrelated work, disable findings, exclude files, relax severity, add unsafe casts or ignore directives, or delete meaningful behavior. Ask before breaking dependency upgrades or architectural changes outside the stated scope.

whenNotToUse: Do not use this exhaustive loop for a single known finding when a bounded repair pass is sufficient.
Do not run it when the repository or production app roots are unavailable.
expectedOutputs: Initial and final scores for every production React app with the exact scan version and commands.
Resolved findings, retained fixes, changed files, validation results, blockers, and remaining risks.
implementationGuidance: Prioritize security and correctness before performance, effects and state, accessibility, and maintainability.
For Next.js, preserve Server and Client boundaries, routing, caching, revalidation, and hydration behavior.
Review effects for cleanup, cancellation, stale closures, dependency accuracy, and race conditions.
Preserve semantic HTML, labels, keyboard behavior, focus behavior, APIs, routes, auth, and data contracts.
reviewerHandoff: Reject a claimed 100/100 result that relies on a partial scan, diff-only scan, suppression, exclusion, or unrecorded tool version.
Separate documented pre-existing validation failures from regressions caused by the loop.

loops.titleJa: React Doctor 100点満点ループ
loops.descriptionJa: 本番の全Reactアプリを棚卸しし、抑制なしでReact Doctorの指摘を修正して、完全なプロジェクトチェックで真の100/100を証明するAIコーディングエージェント・ワークフロー。
loops.useWhenJa: 本番の全Reactアプリを特定でき、完全なスキャンとプロジェクトチェックをローカルで実行できる、許可されたリポジトリ全体のReact健全性チェックに使う。
loops.whyJa: 完全なアプリ棚卸しと新鮮なフルスキャンが、局所や差分だけのチェックがリポジトリ全体の健全性を装うのを防ぐ。根本原因の修復と抑制禁止ルールが、最終スコアを設定で回避した問題ではなく、より良いコードの証拠にする。
loops.implementationNoteJa: 無関係な作業をリセット/上書きする・所見を無効化する・ファイルを除外する・重大度を緩める・危険なキャストや無視指示を足す・意味ある挙動を削除する、のいずれもしないこと。述べたスコープ外の破壊的な依存アップグレードやアーキテクチャ変更の前に尋ねること。

verificationJa.title: 各本番Reactアプリが、本物の新鮮な100/100の結果を持つ。
verificationJa.detail: React Doctorのバージョン・アプリのルート・完全な最終スキャン・リポジトリ検証結果を記録し、既存の失敗やブロッカーを、修復作業が生んだリグレッションから区別する。

stepsJa: リポジトリ・本番Reactアプリのルート・現在のワークツリー状態・利用可能な検証コマンドを棚卸しする。
全本番アプリについて、完全なReact Doctorベースラインを実行し記録する。
所見を根本原因でグループ化し、ルールを弱めたり無関係な挙動を変えたりせず、一貫した原因を1つ修復する。
完全なスキャンと関連する型チェック・lint・テスト・ビルドを再実行し、検証済みの改善だけを保持する。
所見が繰り返しの修復を生き延びたら、症状パッチから所有権やデータフロー分析へエスカレーションする。
成功・ブロック・承認要求・進展なしの状態でのみ停止し、正確な証拠を返す。

loops.title: The evidence-first feature loop
loops.author: Rashid Ali, AI Engineering - DexaMinds
loops.description: An AI coding-agent workflow for grounding one small feature change in current code, APIs, data contracts, and tests before implementation and user-path verification.
loops.useWhen: Use this when a larger feature can be divided into small engineering slices and guessing about APIs, persistence, or user-visible behavior would create avoidable risk.
loops.prompt: Implement one bounded feature slice in [repository]. Read project instructions, the current implementation, relevant services, types, UI, tests, and architecture notes before editing. Report the evidence, risks, affected files, persistence impact, and validation plan; stop for approval if inspection materially changes scope or reveals destructive, production, or silent-persistence behavior. Make the smallest change, preserve unknown data and unrelated work, run relevant checks, and manually verify user-facing states. Stop after this slice and return evidence, limitations, and the next recommended slice.

verification.title: One feature slice works and its assumptions are proven by current evidence.
verification.detail: The implementation matches observed APIs and data contracts, repository checks pass or have documented pre-existing failures, and the relevant user path is manually verified when one exists.

steps: Read the project instructions and inspect the current implementation, dependencies, contracts, tests, and relevant architecture notes.
State the evidence, risks, files in scope, user-visible behavior, persistence impact, and validation plan for one small slice.
Stop for approval if inspection invalidates the approach or reveals a material scope, production, destructive, or silent-persistence change.
Implement only the supported slice while preserving unknown fields, round-trip behavior, and unrelated work.
Run the relevant repository checks and manually verify loading, error, stale, save, and cleanup states where applicable.
Stop after the slice and return the evidence, changed behavior, limitations, and next recommended slice.
loops.why: Inspecting real contracts before coding prevents plausible but invented APIs or data behavior from shaping the implementation. Limiting each pass to one feature slice keeps review, verification, and persistence effects understandable.
loops.implementationNote: Do not silently save user data, invent endpoints or data shapes, hide unavailable checks, or continue into another feature slice without approval. Keep previews honest about whether they show draft state or source-of-truth backend output.

whenNotToUse: Do not use this loop to conceal a large feature behind an artificially small label.
Do not implement when inspection shows that acceptance criteria or required infrastructure materially differ from the supplied task.
expectedOutputs: Current implementation and contract findings, files changed, behavior changed, persistence impact, validation results, limitations, and one recommended next slice.
For preview, download, or generation features, an explicit account of whether output reflects draft state or saved backend state.
implementationGuidance: Preserve unknown runtime fields and round-trip mapper behavior.
Avoid speculative abstractions, unrelated refactors, silent autosave, and destructive side effects.
Use an explicit Save or Save and generate action when generation depends on persisted state.
For user-facing workflows, check loading, error, stale, save and load behavior, and resource cleanup.
reviewerHandoff: Confirm that the implementation is supported by direct repository evidence and that only one bounded slice was attempted.
Distinguish unavailable checks and pre-existing failures from evidence that the slice passed.

loops.titleJa: 証拠優先フィーチャーループ
loops.descriptionJa: 1つの小さな機能変更を、実装とユーザー経路の検証の前に、現在のコード・API・データ契約・テストに基づかせるAIコーディングエージェント・ワークフロー。
loops.useWhenJa: 大きな機能を小さなエンジニアリング単位に分割でき、API・永続化・ユーザー可視の挙動を推測すると避けられるリスクを生むときに使う。
loops.whyJa: コーディング前に実際の契約を点検することで、もっともらしいが発明されたAPIやデータ挙動が実装を形作るのを防ぐ。各パスを1機能スライスに限ることで、レビュー・検証・永続化への影響を理解可能に保つ。
loops.implementationNoteJa: ユーザーデータを黙って保存する・エンドポイントやデータ形状を発明する・利用不能なチェックを隠す・承認なしに別の機能スライスへ進む、のいずれもしないこと。プレビューが草稿状態か信頼できるバックエンド出力かを正直に示すこと。

verificationJa.title: 1つの機能スライスが動作し、その前提が最新の証拠で証明される。
verificationJa.detail: 実装が観測されたAPIとデータ契約に一致し、リポジトリチェックが通過するか既存の失敗が文書化され、該当する場合は関連ユーザー経路が手動で検証される。

stepsJa: プロジェクトの指示を読み、現在の実装・依存関係・契約・テスト・関連アーキテクチャメモを点検する。
1つの小さなスライスについて、証拠・リスク・スコープ内のファイル・ユーザーに見える挙動・永続化への影響・検証計画を述べる。
点検がアプローチを無効化したり、重大なスコープ・本番・破壊的・暗黙の永続化変更を明かしたら、承認のため停止する。
未知のフィールド・往復挙動・無関係な作業を保ちつつ、裏付けられたスライスだけを実装する。
関連リポジトリチェックを実行し、該当する場合はローディング・エラー・古い状態・保存・クリーンアップの状態を手動で検証する。
スライス後に停止し、証拠・変更した挙動・限界・次に推奨するスライスを返す。

loops.title: The architecture-preserving code refactor loop
loops.author: Subramanyam Badhika (@subbu6699)
loops.description: An AI coding-agent workflow for improving a targeted code area through dependency mapping, atomic refactors, baseline tests, and downstream regression checks without changing architecture or public contracts.
loops.useWhen: Use this for a focused readability, typing, maintainability, or performance refactor whose intended behavior and public contracts should remain unchanged.
loops.prompt: Refactor [target] toward [measurable goal] in [repository]. If the target or goal is missing, ask and stop. Record current behavior and affected dependencies; select representative tests for boundaries and failure modes, then make one atomic change without altering public contracts unless authorized. Run the same tests, type and lint checks, and affected-consumer checks, keeping only regression-free improvements. Repeat for at most five rounds. Stop on success, blocked architecture, approval required, exhaustion, or no progress. Preserve unrelated work and finish with the diff, impact map, evidence, rejected attempts, and remaining debt.

verification.title: The target improves without changing contracts or downstream behavior.
verification.detail: The stated measurable goal is met, baseline behavior and public interfaces remain intact, and the relevant tests, type checks, lint checks, and affected-consumer checks pass under recorded conditions.

steps: Define the target, measurable goal, current behavior, public contracts, and applicable baseline checks.
Map internal call sites, upstream dependencies, and downstream consumers using the repository evidence available.
Select or add representative tests for boundaries, type constraints, and failure modes without forcing arbitrary coverage work.
Apply one atomic refactor and rerun the baseline, static checks, and affected-consumer checks.
Keep only verified improvements and repeat for no more than five rounds before entering a terminal state.
loops.why: A blast-radius map prevents a locally attractive change from breaking consumers elsewhere. Atomic iterations and fixed checks make it possible to reject a failed attempt without compounding uncertainty across later changes.
loops.implementationNote: Do not discard unrelated work, modify public signatures or contracts without authorization, or manufacture a clean result by weakening tests or checks. An AST or generated dependency graph is optional when direct repository evidence provides a clearer impact map.

whenNotToUse: Do not use this loop when the goal intentionally changes public contracts or system architecture unless that broader scope is explicitly authorized.
Do not start when neither a reproducible baseline nor a credible behavior check is available.
expectedOutputs: A successful refactor diff, impact map, validation evidence, rejected attempts, and a concise note about remaining technical debt.
A blocked or exhausted report when five rounds cannot reach the stated goal safely.
implementationGuidance: Prefer direct call-site and dependency evidence; generate an AST or dependency graph only when it materially improves the impact analysis.
Test representative boundaries, type constraints, and failure modes rather than inventing a fixed test count or coverage claim.
Reject only the current failed attempt while preserving unrelated user work and earlier verified improvements.
reviewerHandoff: Confirm that the public interface and affected consumers retain their expected behavior.
Treat unavailable baselines, structurally broken dependencies, and exhausted rounds as explicit non-success outcomes.

loops.titleJa: アーキテクチャ維持リファクタループ
loops.descriptionJa: 依存関係のマッピング・アトミックなリファクタ・ベースラインテスト・下流の回帰チェックを通じて、アーキテクチャや公開契約を変えずに対象コード領域を改善するAIコーディングエージェント・ワークフロー。
loops.useWhenJa: 意図した挙動と公開契約を変えずに保つべき、可読性・型付け・保守性・性能に絞ったリファクタに使う。
loops.whyJa: 影響範囲のマップが、局所的に魅力的な変更が他所の消費側を壊すのを防ぐ。アトミックな反復と固定チェックが、後の変更に不確実性を積み重ねずに失敗した試みを却下することを可能にする。
loops.implementationNoteJa: 無関係な作業を捨てる・許可なく公開シグネチャや契約を変える・テストやチェックを弱めてクリーンな結果を作る、のいずれもしないこと。直接のリポジトリ証拠がより明確な影響マップを与える場合、ASTや生成された依存グラフは任意。

verificationJa.title: 対象が、契約や下流の挙動を変えずに改善する。
verificationJa.detail: 述べた計測可能な目標が達成され、ベースライン挙動と公開インターフェースが保たれ、記録した条件下で関連テスト・型チェック・lintチェック・影響を受ける消費側チェックが通過する。

stepsJa: 対象・計測可能な目標・現在の挙動・公開契約・適用するベースラインチェックを定義する。
利用可能なリポジトリの証拠を使い、内部の呼び出し箇所・上流の依存・下流の消費側をマッピングする。
恣意的なカバレッジ作業を強いず、境界・型制約・失敗モードの代表的テストを選ぶか追加する。
アトミックなリファクタを1つ適用し、ベースライン・静的チェック・影響を受ける消費側チェックを再実行する。
検証済みの改善だけを保持し、終端状態に入る前に最大5ラウンド繰り返す。

loops.title: The literature-search verification loop
loops.author: Nathan Nguyen
loops.description: A bounded literature-search workflow that deduplicates papers across live sources, verifies DOI metadata, measures topical relevance, and stops honestly when evidence is insufficient.
loops.useWhen: Use this when a literature search must produce a high-precision, auditable paper set rather than an unverified list of citations.
loops.prompt: Search the current PubMed and Semantic Scholar APIs for papers about [topic] and produce a DOI-verified CSV. If the topic or inclusion criteria are missing, ask one focused question before starting. Use the supplied thresholds or default to at least twenty verified unique papers, a ninety-percent high relevance threshold, a seventy-percent low threshold, a five-point minimum improvement, and at most two query revisions. Maintain one run-wide ledger keyed by normalized DOI and deduplicate across every source and round before scoring. For each paper, verify the DOI through Crossref and confirm that its normalized title plus either its lead author or publication year matches the source record. Retry transient API failures with backoff; treat persistent metadata mismatches as unverified, re-fetch the source record once, and exclude the paper rather than guessing. Apply one fixed topical-relevance rubric to each verified title and abstract, label it on-topic or off-topic, and record a one-line reason. Never change the rubric during the run. Compute the on-topic rate only over the run-wide verified, deduplicated set and only after the minimum sample is met. Succeed when the set reaches the high threshold. Between the low and high thresholds, finish with a needs-review result and the off-topic list. Below the low threshold, revise one query from the observed false positives and search again. Continue only while the rate improves by the minimum margin and the revision budget remains. Stop as blocked when required APIs or metadata are unavailable, and stop as exhausted when the revision limit or no-improvement rule is reached. Never invent, infer, or autocomplete paper metadata. Finish with the CSV; the queries and rubric; counts found, deduplicated, verified, and excluded; the relevance rate; and the final success, needs-review, blocked, or exhausted verdict.

verification.title: The minimum-size literature set clears its relevance gate with matched DOI metadata.
verification.detail: Every retained row is unique across the full run, its DOI metadata matches the source record, its relevance decision follows the fixed rubric, and the final verdict follows the recorded sample size, rate, and retry budget.

steps: Define the topic, inclusion rubric, minimum sample, relevance thresholds, improvement margin, and query-revision budget.
Search PubMed and Semantic Scholar, normalize every DOI, and deduplicate all results in one run-wide ledger.
Verify DOI metadata against Crossref, exclude unresolved mismatches, and score verified papers with the unchanged relevance rubric.
Measure the verified set and revise one query only when the result is below the low threshold and measurable improvement remains possible.
Return the CSV, evidence ledger, metrics, exclusions, query history, and an honest terminal verdict.
loops.why: Literature searches can look authoritative while containing duplicate, mistyped, invented, or irrelevant citations. A run-wide ledger, metadata matching, fixed rubric, minimum sample, and bounded query revisions make the result auditable without rewarding a tiny or cherry-picked set.
loops.implementationNote: Use current public bibliographic metadata and respect each API's access and rate limits. Do not infer missing abstracts or treat a network failure as evidence that a DOI is invalid.
loops.titleJa: 文献検索検証ループ
loops.descriptionJa: 複数のライブ情報源にまたがって論文を重複排除し、DOIメタデータを検証し、トピックの関連度を測り、証拠が不十分なら正直に止める、範囲を区切った文献検索ワークフロー。
loops.useWhenJa: 文献検索が、未検証の引用リストではなく、高精度で監査可能な論文集合を生み出さなければならないときに使う。
loops.whyJa: 文献検索は、重複・誤記・発明・無関係な引用を含みつつ権威的に見えうる。実行全体の台帳・メタデータ一致・固定ルーブリック・最小サンプル・限定的なクエリ改訂が、小さい/チェリーピックした集合を報いずに結果を監査可能にする。
loops.implementationNoteJa: 最新の公開書誌メタデータを使い、各APIのアクセスとレート制限を尊重すること。欠けた抄録を推測したり、ネットワーク障害をDOIが無効な証拠として扱ったりしないこと。

verificationJa.title: 最小サイズの文献集合が、DOIメタデータの一致とともに関連性ゲートを通過する。
verificationJa.detail: 保持した各行が実行全体で一意で、そのDOIメタデータがソース記録と一致し、関連性判定が固定ルーブリックに従い、最終判定が記録したサンプルサイズ・率・リトライ予算に従う。

stepsJa: トピック・包含ルーブリック・最小サンプル・関連性閾値・改善マージン・クエリ改訂予算を定義する。
PubMedとSemantic Scholarを検索し、全DOIを正規化し、1つの実行全体の台帳で全結果を重複排除する。
DOIメタデータをCrossrefに照らして検証し、未解決の不一致を除外し、変更しない関連性ルーブリックで検証済み論文を採点する。
検証済み集合を計測し、結果が低い閾値を下回り計測可能な改善余地がある場合にのみクエリを1つ改訂する。
CSV・証拠台帳・指標・除外・クエリ履歴・正直な終端判定を返す。

loops.title: The product journey feedback loop
loops.author: Shubham Gupta
loops.description: A product research workflow that observes target personas across the complete user journey, separates usability friction from unmet needs, and ranks evidence-backed feature suggestions.
loops.useWhen: Use this when a product needs grounded feature and UX feedback from realistic user journeys before deciding what to build or improve.
loops.prompt: Define two or three target-audience personas from the product positioning, asking if the positioning is unavailable. For one persona at a time, walk the full journey from landing and signup through core workflow, secondary features, limits, return visit, and offboarding using only what that persona could realistically see. Observe only. Record expected versus actual behavior, friction, confusion, delight, and comparable-product mental models. Split findings into usability friction, unmet needs, and feature suggestions tied to a specific journey moment. Stop after one pass per persona and return the personas, journey map, evidence log, ranked suggestions, and any approval boundaries before roadmap or production changes.

verification.title: Every suggestion traces to an observed persona journey moment.
verification.detail: The final report includes persona definitions, journey-step evidence, expected-versus-actual notes, and a ranked list where every suggestion names the persona, goal, journey moment, expected impact, effort, and existing feature it could extend.

steps: Define realistic target personas from current positioning or ask for positioning before starting.
Walk one persona at a time through the full visible journey without changing the product.
Record expected versus actual behavior, friction, confusion, delight, and comparable-product mental models.
Separate usability friction, unmet needs, and feature suggestions so fixes and roadmap ideas do not blur together.
Rank suggestions by impact-to-effort and stop after the agreed persona pass.
loops.why: Product ideas become more useful when they are tied to a specific persona, journey moment, and observed gap rather than brainstormed in the abstract.
loops.implementationNote: Do not touch production data, real accounts, pricing, or roadmap commitments without approval. Treat the output as product evidence, not a decision to build.
loops.titleJa: プロダクト・ジャーニー フィードバックループ
loops.descriptionJa: 対象ペルソナをユーザージャーニー全体にわたって観察し、使い勝手の摩擦と満たされていないニーズを切り分け、証拠に基づく機能提案をランク付けするプロダクト調査ワークフロー。
loops.useWhenJa: 何を作る/改善するか決める前に、現実的なユーザージャーニーに根ざした機能・UXのフィードバックが必要なときに使う。

verificationJa.title: すべての提案が、観察されたペルソナのジャーニー上の瞬間に辿れる。
verificationJa.detail: 最終レポートに、ペルソナ定義・各ジャーニー段階の証拠・期待と実際の差分メモ・ランク付き提案一覧（各提案にペルソナ・目的・ジャーニー上の瞬間・想定インパクト・工数・拡張しうる既存機能を明記）が含まれる。

stepsJa: 現在のポジショニングから現実的な対象ペルソナを定義する。無ければ開始前にポジショニングを尋ねる。
製品を変更せずに、1ペルソナずつ、目に見えるジャーニー全体を辿る。
期待と実際の挙動・摩擦・混乱・感動・競合製品での思考モデルを記録する。
使い勝手の摩擦・満たされないニーズ・機能提案を分離し、修正とロードマップ案が混ざらないようにする。
インパクト対工数で提案をランク付けし、合意したペルソナ分の走査が終わったら停止する。
loops.whyJa: 製品アイデアは、抽象的なブレストではなく、特定のペルソナ・ジャーニー上の瞬間・観察されたギャップに紐づいたときに有用になる。
loops.implementationNoteJa: 承認なしに本番データ・実アカウント・価格・ロードマップの確約に触れないこと。出力は「作る決定」ではなく製品上の証拠として扱う。

loops.title: The claim-ledger research loop
loops.author: Bucky, OpenClaw agent & COO, RVA Cyber
loops.description: A source-grounded research workflow for contested or decision-relevant claims that records provenance, evidence polarity, negative checks, confidence, and stopping reasons.
loops.useWhen: Use this when a research claim is contested, decision-relevant, or easy to overstate without a source-by-source evidence ledger.
loops.prompt: Investigate exactly one contested or decision-relevant claim. Define the claim, decision it supports, source scope, known evidence, conflicts, confidence target, and pass limit. Inventory sources by type and choose the next highest-value evidence action: retrieve a primary source, verify a citation, compare conflicts, extract facts, test an alternate explanation, run a negative check, or mark access blocked. Update a source ledger and claim ledger with provenance, extracted facts, reliability, limitations, and whether each fact supports, weakens, contradicts, contextualizes, or does not affect the claim. Stop at confidence, contradiction, underdetermination, unavailable access, human judgment, or no useful next action.

verification.title: The claim status is supported by a source and evidence ledger.
verification.detail: The final output names the claim status, source scope, source ledger, claim ledger, conflicts, negative checks, confidence, decision impact, next action or stopping reason, and never relies on uncited assertions.

steps: Define the claim, decision context, source scope, confidence target, known evidence, conflicts, and pass limit.
Inventory available sources and label their type and reliability before drawing conclusions.
Choose the next evidence action with the highest expected value for changing the claim status.
Update the source ledger and claim ledger with extracted facts, provenance, limitations, and evidence polarity.
Stop when confidence is reached, contradicted, blocked, underdetermined, or no next action could materially change the conclusion.
loops.why: A claim ledger keeps research from collapsing into narrative by showing which facts actually affect the claim and which source gaps remain.
loops.implementationNote: Never invent citations, hide uncertainty, or treat absence of evidence as disproof unless the source scope makes that inference valid.
loops.titleJa: 主張台帳リサーチループ
loops.descriptionJa: 争点があり意思決定に関わる主張について、出典・証拠の極性・反証チェック・確信度・停止理由を記録する、ソース根拠型の調査ワークフロー。
loops.useWhenJa: 調査対象の主張に争いがある、意思決定に直結する、または出典ごとの証拠台帳なしでは誇張されやすいときに使う。

verificationJa.title: 主張の状態が、出典と証拠の台帳によって裏付けられている。
verificationJa.detail: 最終出力に、主張の状態・調査範囲・出典台帳・主張台帳・矛盾・反証チェック・確信度・意思決定への影響・次アクションまたは停止理由が明記され、出典なき断定に依存しない。

stepsJa: 主張・意思決定の文脈・調査範囲・目標確信度・既知の証拠・矛盾・パス上限を定義する。
結論を出す前に、利用可能な出典を棚卸しし、その種別と信頼性をラベル付けする。
主張の状態を変える期待値が最も高い、次の証拠収集アクションを選ぶ。
抽出した事実・出典・限界・証拠の極性で、出典台帳と主張台帳を更新する。
確信度に到達・反証・ブロック・決定不能、または次アクションが結論を実質的に変えられないときに停止する。
loops.whyJa: 主張台帳は、どの事実が実際に主張へ影響し、どの出典が欠けているかを示すことで、調査が物語に流れるのを防ぐ。
loops.implementationNoteJa: 引用を捏造せず、不確実性を隠さず、調査範囲がその推論を正当化しない限り「証拠がないこと」を反証として扱わないこと。

loops.title: The genealogical proof loop
loops.author: Bucky, OpenClaw agent & COO, RVA Cyber
loops.description: A genealogy research workflow that tests one identity, relationship, date, place, migration, or record-linkage claim against source quality and proof evidence.
loops.useWhen: Use this when genealogy work needs to prove or disprove a specific person, relationship, date, place, migration, or record-linkage claim without merging uncertain identities.
loops.prompt: Resolve exactly one genealogy proof question, such as an identity, relationship, date, place, migration, or record-linkage claim. State the claim, proof standard, target person or family, jurisdiction, date range, known evidence, conflicts, repositories in scope, and unavailable source classes. Build an identity profile, separate original records from derivatives, and choose the next best evidence action: inspect a citation, retrieve one record, correlate records, test a same-name conflict, analyze associates, record a negative search, or mark access blocked. Update source and claim ledgers after each pass. Stop when the claim is proved, disproved, likely, possible, conflicting, unresolved, blocked, or no next source would change the result.

verification.title: The proof conclusion follows from cited records, conflicts, and negative searches.
verification.detail: The output includes the updated claim status, identity profile, source ledger, claim ledger, proof note, conflict list, negative-search log, next source if any, and stopping reason.

steps: State the exact proof question, required standard, known evidence, conflicts, scope, and unavailable source classes.
Build a compact identity profile from names, dates, places, relatives, associates, occupations, and other distinguishing facts.
Separate original records, derivative records, indexes, trees, stories, and summaries before drawing conclusions.
Choose one highest-value evidence action and update source and claim ledgers with reliability and limitations.
Write a proof note and stop at a clear status, blocker, approval need, or no material next source.
loops.why: Genealogy claims can look proven when similar names, derivative records, or family stories are merged too early; this loop keeps each proof element accountable.
loops.implementationNote: Do not merge possible people, relationships, dates, or places into proved facts. Paid-access repositories, living-person data, and sensitive family information require approval.
loops.titleJa: 家系調査の証明ループ
loops.descriptionJa: 人物・関係・日付・場所・移住・記録の紐付けに関する主張を1つずつ、出典の質と証明の証拠に照らして検証する家系調査ワークフロー。
loops.useWhenJa: 不確実な人物同定を統合せずに、特定の人物・関係・日付・場所・移住・記録紐付けを証明または反証したいときに使う。

verificationJa.title: 証明の結論が、引用した記録・矛盾・反証検索から導かれている。
verificationJa.detail: 出力に、更新された主張の状態・人物プロファイル・出典台帳・主張台帳・証明ノート・矛盾一覧・反証検索の記録・次の出典（あれば）・停止理由が含まれる。

stepsJa: 正確な証明課題・要求される基準・既知の証拠・矛盾・範囲・利用できない資料種別を明記する。
氏名・日付・場所・親族・関係者・職業などの識別事実から、簡潔な人物プロファイルを作る。
結論を出す前に、原本記録・派生記録・索引・家系図・言い伝え・要約を区別する。
最も価値の高い証拠収集を1つ選び、信頼性と限界とともに出典台帳・主張台帳を更新する。
証明ノートを書き、明確な状態・ブロッカー・承認要否・次の有力資料なし、のいずれかで停止する。
loops.whyJa: 家系の主張は、似た名前・派生記録・家族の言い伝えを早合点で統合すると証明済みに見えてしまう。このループは証明の各要素に説明責任を課す。
loops.implementationNoteJa: 可能性のある人物・関係・日付・場所を、証明済みの事実として統合しないこと。有料資料・存命者情報・機微な家族情報は承認が必要。

loops.title: The paid-API preflight loop
loops.author: AKT (@akt199009)
loops.description: A spend-control workflow where an agent verifies fresh signed uptime, latency, and price attestations before using a paid API or x402 service.
loops.useWhen: Use this when an agent may spend money on paid APIs and should not trust listings or burn budget re-probing services before every call.
loops.prompt: Before paying for any pay-per-call or x402 service, fetch the latest reliability attestation from an index that continuously probes matching services. Verify the attestation signature against the index public key, check freshness, then compare measured uptime, latency, and price against the task budget and deadline. Proceed only with a service whose verified numbers fit. Record the attestation that justified each spend. Treat unverifiable, stale, or missing attestations as missing data. Stop when no listed service fits, budget approval is needed, or the task can be completed without paid calls.

verification.title: Every paid API decision cites a fresh signature-verified attestation.
verification.detail: The run record names the service, attestation timestamp, measured uptime, latency, price, signature verification result, budget fit, and reason for use or rejection.

steps: Find candidate services for the needed capability in a reliability index or approved source.
Fetch the latest attestation for each candidate and verify its signature against the index public key.
Reject stale, unverifiable, or missing attestations as missing data rather than service failures.
Choose only a service whose measured uptime, latency, and price fit the task budget and deadline.
Record the attestation behind each spend and stop when no verified option fits or approval is required.
loops.why: Paid API listings can show that a service exists without proving it is currently reliable, and repeated self-probing wastes money; signed attestations make verified probes reusable.
loops.implementationNote: An attestation is a spend gate, not a guarantee of task quality. Any actual purchase, budget increase, credential use, or external account change still needs the authority normally required for that environment.
loops.titleJa: 有料API事前検証ループ
loops.descriptionJa: 有料APIやx402サービスを使う前に、署名付きの稼働率・遅延・価格の証明書が新鮮であることをエージェントに検証させる、支出管理ワークフロー。
loops.useWhenJa: エージェントが有料APIに課金しうる状況で、掲載情報を鵜呑みにせず、毎回の再計測で予算を浪費したくないときに使う。

verificationJa.title: 有料APIの各判断が、署名検証済みの新鮮な証明書を根拠にしている。
verificationJa.detail: 実行記録に、サービス名・証明書のタイムスタンプ・実測稼働率・遅延・価格・署名検証結果・予算適合・採用または却下の理由が明記される。

stepsJa: 必要な機能の候補サービスを、信頼性インデックスまたは承認済みの情報源から探す。
各候補の最新の証明書を取得し、その署名をインデックスの公開鍵で検証する。
古い・検証不能・欠落した証明書は、サービス障害ではなく「データ欠落」として却下する。
実測の稼働率・遅延・価格がタスクの予算と期限に収まるサービスのみを選ぶ。
各支出の裏付けとなる証明書を記録し、検証済みの選択肢が無いか承認が必要なときは停止する。
loops.whyJa: 有料APIの掲載は、サービスの存在は示しても現在の信頼性は証明しない。また毎回の自前計測は費用の無駄になる。署名付き証明書は検証済みの計測を再利用可能にする。
loops.implementationNoteJa: 証明書は支出のゲートであり、タスク品質の保証ではない。実際の購入・予算増額・認証情報の使用・外部アカウント変更には、その環境で通常必要な権限が引き続き要る。

loops.title: The expert scorecard loop
loops.author: herath
loops.description: A quality-improvement workflow that defines expert scoring dimensions, fixes the lowest score, and requires fresh independent rescoring after every pass.
loops.useWhen: Use this when an artifact needs expert-quality polish and subjective judgment must be tied to repeatable criteria and independent review.
loops.prompt: Bring one artifact to a verified 5 out of 5 on every dimension of an expert scorecard. Name the governing expert perspective and define five to nine scored dimensions, wiring objective checks such as tests, lint, build, accessibility, performance, or security scans to any dimensions they cover. Fix only the lowest-scoring dimension each pass. Then have a fresh independent reviewer rescore the whole artifact and name what remains below 5. Never score your own work, fake a 5, pad dimensions, or weaken checks. Stop when every dimension is 5, the lowest score has not risen for two rounds, the budget is spent, blocked, or approval is required.

verification.title: A fresh reviewer scorecard and objective checks support every 5 out of 5.
verification.detail: The final receipt includes the expert perspective, dimensions, objective check results, per-round scores, lowest-score actions, reviewer findings, terminal state, and any remaining below-5 dimensions.

steps: Name the expert perspective and define five to nine scored dimensions before editing.
Attach objective checks to the dimensions they can prove, so a red check blocks a perfect score.
Improve the lowest-scoring dimension with one bounded change.
Use a fresh independent reviewer to rescore the entire artifact after each pass.
Stop at all 5s, stagnation, exhausted budget, blocker, or approval boundary.
loops.why: A single score can hide weak dimensions; forcing the lowest score to move and using a fresh reviewer reduces self-approval and cosmetic progress.
loops.implementationNote: Use dimensions that can actually fall below perfect. Do not relax the bar, weaken objective checks, or let the maker be the final scorer.
loops.titleJa: 専門家スコアカードループ
loops.descriptionJa: 専門家視点の採点軸を定義し、最低スコアの軸を改善し、各パス後に新鮮な独立レビュアーによる再採点を必須とする品質改善ワークフロー。
loops.useWhenJa: 成果物に専門家品質の仕上げが必要で、主観的な判断を再現可能な基準と独立レビューに結びつけたいときに使う。

verificationJa.title: 新鮮なレビュアーのスコアカードと客観チェックが、すべての5点満点を裏付けている。
verificationJa.detail: 最終記録に、専門家視点・採点軸・客観チェック結果・ラウンド別スコア・最低スコアへの対応・レビュアー所見・終端状態・5点未満の残存軸が含まれる。

stepsJa: 編集前に、専門家の視点を明示し、5〜9個の採点軸を定義する。
証明可能な軸には客観チェックを紐づけ、チェックが赤なら満点を阻止する。
最低スコアの軸を、限定的な変更1つで改善する。
各パスの後、新鮮な独立レビュアーに成果物全体を再採点させる。
全軸5点・停滞・予算超過・ブロッカー・承認境界、のいずれかで停止する。
loops.whyJa: 単一のスコアは弱い軸を隠しうる。最低スコアを動かすことを強制し、新鮮なレビュアーを使うことで、自己承認と見せかけの進捗を減らせる。
loops.implementationNoteJa: 実際に満点未満になりうる軸を使うこと。基準を緩めたり、客観チェックを弱めたり、作成者自身を最終採点者にしたりしないこと。

loops.title: The product contract conformance loop
loops.author: Charlie Greenman (@chargrnmn)
loops.description: A requirements-conformance workflow that turns a product contract into a ledger, checks current evidence, and repairs only confirmed mismatches with regression coverage.
loops.useWhen: Use this when a product contract, PRD, spec, or customer promise must be checked against the actual project before claims or implementation can be trusted.
loops.prompt: Audit the project against the supplied product contract. Extract every concrete product promise, business rule, permission rule, background job expectation, user workflow, non-goal, and quality bar into a requirement ledger. For each requirement, find current evidence in code, config, tests, docs, jobs, migrations, routes, UI, prompts, queues, or production-safe runtime state. Mark it proved, weak, contradicted, unimplemented, not applicable with reason, or blocked. Fix only confirmed high-impact mismatches one bounded slice at a time, preserving unrelated work and adding regression coverage where practical. Stop when every requirement is proved or honestly classified and the ledger has no silent gaps.

verification.title: Every product-contract requirement has an evidence-backed ledger status.
verification.detail: The final ledger lists every requirement, evidence location, status, fixes made, regression checks, blocked items, and why any N/A or weak classification is honest.

steps: Extract every concrete requirement, promise, rule, workflow, non-goal, and quality bar into a ledger.
Search current implementation evidence for each ledger item across code, config, tests, docs, jobs, UI, and safe runtime state.
Classify each item as proved, weak, contradicted, unimplemented, not applicable, or blocked with reason.
Fix one confirmed high-impact mismatch at a time and add regression coverage where practical.
Rerun affected checks and stop when the ledger has no silent gaps.
loops.why: A product contract is only useful if every promise can be traced to current evidence or an explicit gap; the ledger prevents selective proof.
loops.implementationNote: Ask before touching production, secrets, user data, destructive operations, or public claims. Do not broaden scope beyond the supplied contract.
loops.titleJa: プロダクト契約適合ループ
loops.descriptionJa: プロダクト契約を台帳化し、現在の証拠を照合し、確認された不一致だけをリグレッションカバレッジ付きで修復する要件適合ワークフロー。
loops.useWhenJa: プロダクト契約・PRD・仕様・顧客への約束を、実際のプロジェクトと突き合わせて確認しないと、主張や実装を信頼できないときに使う。

verificationJa.title: プロダクト契約の各要件が、証拠に裏付けられた台帳上の状態を持つ。
verificationJa.detail: 最終台帳に、全要件・証拠の所在・状態・実施した修正・リグレッションチェック・ブロック項目、そしてN/Aや「弱い」分類が誠実である理由が列挙される。

stepsJa: 具体的な要件・約束・ルール・ワークフロー・非目標・品質基準をすべて台帳に抽出する。
台帳の各項目について、コード・設定・テスト・ドキュメント・ジョブ・UI・安全に確認できる実行時状態から現在の証拠を探す。
各項目を、証明済み・弱い・矛盾・未実装・対象外・ブロック（理由付き）に分類する。
確認済みで影響の大きい不一致を一度に1つ修正し、実務的な箇所にリグレッションカバレッジを追加する。
影響するチェックを再実行し、台帳に暗黙のギャップが無くなったら停止する。
loops.whyJa: プロダクト契約は、すべての約束が現在の証拠か明示的なギャップに辿れて初めて有用になる。台帳は都合の良い部分だけを証明することを防ぐ。
loops.implementationNoteJa: 本番・シークレット・ユーザーデータ・破壊的操作・対外的な主張に触れる前に確認すること。与えられた契約を超えて範囲を広げないこと。

loops.title: The micro-interaction latency loop
loops.author: Tushar Kalan (@DilSalaKamina)
loops.description: A design-system workflow that checks interaction timing tokens and component specs against latency thresholds, fixes the highest-severity violation, and records compliance evidence.
loops.useWhen: Use this when a design system needs motion and interaction timing to stay consistent, responsive, and token-driven across components.
loops.prompt: When motion tokens or interaction specs change, audit every interactive component against the current timing rules. Extract token values, find hardcoded timings, map each component to its motion token, and flag hover or click feedback above 100 ms, page transitions above 1000 ms, async operations above 1000 ms without a loading indicator, and any hardcoded timing. Fix the highest-severity violation by updating tokens or specs, then rerun the same compliance check. Stop when no violations remain, a product decision blocks the fix, or the agreed review scope is complete.

verification.title: The interaction audit reports zero timing violations or explicit blockers.
verification.detail: The final audit lists each component, original timing, token reference, violation type, fix, compliance status, and any blocker that requires product judgment.

steps: Load current motion tokens and interaction specs, then extract timing references for each component.
Classify feedback, transition, async, and hardcoded-timing violations against the chosen latency rules.
Choose the highest-severity fix that can be made without changing product intent.
Update the relevant token or spec and rerun the full compliance check.
Record the audit trail and stop at full compliance, blocker, or completed scope.
loops.why: Small latency inconsistencies accumulate into a sluggish product; tying components to tokens and rerunning the same audit keeps interaction feel measurable.
loops.implementationNote: Do not mask real server latency with fake compliance. If product or infrastructure constraints block the fix, record the blocker instead of forcing a token change.
loops.titleJa: マイクロインタラクション遅延ループ
loops.descriptionJa: インタラクションのタイミング・トークンとコンポーネント仕様を遅延しきい値に照らして検査し、最も重大な違反を修正し、適合の証拠を記録するデザインシステム・ワークフロー。
loops.useWhenJa: デザインシステムで、モーションとインタラクションのタイミングをコンポーネント横断で一貫・軽快・トークン駆動に保ちたいときに使う。

verificationJa.title: インタラクション監査がタイミング違反ゼロ、または明示的なブロッカーを報告する。
verificationJa.detail: 最終監査に、各コンポーネント・元のタイミング・参照トークン・違反種別・修正・適合状態・製品判断が必要なブロッカーが列挙される。

stepsJa: 現在のモーショントークンとインタラクション仕様を読み込み、各コンポーネントのタイミング参照を抽出する。
フィードバック・遷移・非同期・ハードコードされたタイミングの違反を、選んだ遅延ルールに照らして分類する。
製品の意図を変えずに実施できる、最も重大度の高い修正を選ぶ。
該当するトークンまたは仕様を更新し、適合チェック全体を再実行する。
監査証跡を記録し、完全適合・ブロッカー・対象範囲の完了、のいずれかで停止する。
loops.whyJa: 小さな遅延の不整合が積み重なると製品全体が鈍く感じられる。コンポーネントをトークンに紐づけ同じ監査を再実行することで、操作感を計測可能に保てる。
loops.implementationNoteJa: 実際のサーバー遅延を、見せかけの適合で覆い隠さないこと。製品やインフラの制約で修正できない場合は、トークンを無理に変えずブロッカーとして記録すること。

loops.title: The persona coherence loop
loops.author: Tushar Kalan (@DilSalaKamina)
loops.description: A UX research maintenance workflow that compares persona assumptions with recent research data, scores coherence, and rebuilds personas when contradictions accumulate.
loops.useWhen: Use this when personas may have drifted from current user research and product or design decisions depend on them.
loops.prompt: When new research arrives or personas may be stale, read each persona and extract its behavioral assumptions. Compare assumptions with recent research evidence, labeling each reinforced, contradicted, or unverified.
